% Written by tools/expand.py from rev/; do not edit.
Villagers
An *identity* is a unique cryptographic key pair.
A *party* to a contract is whoever has an identity, and a *person* is a party who established their own identity.
Alice *trusts* Bob when she knows Bob personally and believes him to keep the undertakings he signs under grassroots contracts.
A person is *nearby* Alice when her phone reaches theirs by Bluetooth or the local network, without the Internet; a *place* is where Alice is.
A *message* is what a person sends.
A pointer may be labeled by a person, and a pointer labeled by Dave is a *Dave-pointer*. Friends Alice and Bob have a Bob-pointer from Alice to Bob and an Alice-pointer from Bob to Alice.
A *feed* is named by its author.
A *relation* is a friendship or the membership of a group. Bob *trusts* Wendy, a child of Alice, when he trusts Alice. The *decision rule*, which the creator of a child decides, says who decides for a child and how. A child takes an act of a party by those who decide for the child.
A *broadcast* is a message with a unique identifier, which its maker holds. Δ > 0 is a period of time, and a broadcast is *live* for Δ after it is made.
Bob *trusts* Orga, an organisation of Alice, when he trusts Alice. The *decision rule*, which the creator of an organisation decides, says who decides for an organisation and how. An organisation takes an act of a party by those who decide for the organisation.
An *organisation* is a ward with *participants*, which include its *officers*, each with a *role*. The *bylaws*, which its founder decides, name the roles of an organisation and say who decides each of its acts and how, their own amendment included.
A *personal emergency* is a broadcast that includes the location of its maker, a description and the help its maker asks; it ceases to be live when its maker resolves it. A *village emergency* is a broadcast that includes instructions. A *resolution* of a personal emergency and an *answer* to it are broadcasts.
A *notice* is a broadcast that includes its text and the area it is for.
A *note* includes its issuer's public key and a unique note identifier, is signed by their private key, and gives its holder a right against its issuer. An *Alice-note* is a note issued by Alice.
A *coin* is a note that is a unit of its issuer's debt. An *Alice-coin* is a coin issued by Alice.
A *bond* is a note that is a unit of its issuer's debt, due at its maturity date, which it includes. An *Alice-bond* is a bond issued by Alice. A bond is *mature* when its maturity date is at most the current date.
*Dollar* names one denomination, and a *Dollar-denominated Alice-coin* is an Alice-coin issued as Alice's debt of one Dollar.
A *Dollar-denominated Alice-bond* is an Alice-bond issued as Alice's debt of one Dollar, due at its maturity date.
A *bank* is an organisation whose business is issuing coins and bonds against the coins and bonds it holds.
A *community* is a bank whose coins are Dollar-denominated. The coins it issues are *community coins*. Its bylaws name two roles, *member*, held by every participant, and *treasurer*.
A *constitutional democratic community* is an organisation whose bylaws name one role, *member*, held by every participant, and are *egalitarian*: the rule by which the members decide an act names no member and no other role.
A *democratic community* is a community that is a constitutional democratic community.
*f* is a fraction, 0 ≤ f < 1. Orga's *account* is a bank account in Dollars, held in Orga's name by its treasurers. A treasurer, Alice, is *backed* when the Alice-coins Orga holds are at most the Dollars Alice paid into the account and the coins Alice holds of the other treasurers, leaving out the fraction f of them of whom she holds the most.
The bylaws of an organisation name the role *arbiter*. A *dispute* is a disagreement between two participants of an organisation about an act of the organisation or an undertaking. A *ruling* is the text of an arbiter's decision on a dispute. A dispute is raised once, to one arbiter, and has one ruling, which both parties receive.
A *warning* is a record in an organisation, made by one of its officers, that a participant broke its bylaws or an undertaking; it names the incident and the date it is given. An officer holds at most one warning to a participant at a time, and the participant may answer it once; a warning withdrawn or annulled may be given again of the same incident only if it was not answered. A warning stays when the officer who gave it leaves office, until it is withdrawn or annulled. A warning counts toward expelling the participant only from seven days after it is given, so that he has the time to answer it.
A *work* names a task, its *price* in community coins, its *contractor*, who will do it, and its *supervisor*, an officer of the community. The bylaws name the role *arbiter*.
A *mutual credit society* is a bank whose bylaws name one role, *member*, held by every participant. A member is *in the red* by their coins in circulation less the other persons' coins they hold.
A *community network* is created by a backed community, and uses its community coins. Its bylaws name the role *arbiter*. A *provider* is a member of the community whose *stake*, the community coins they hold, is at least *S*, a number of community coins, and a *customer* is a member of the community who accepts community coins. A *dispute* is over community coins locked between a provider and a customer, on *terms* that set the arbiter's fee.
A *seller* is a provider and a *buyer* a customer. A *listing* names a good, its price in community coins and how it is delivered; its terms say what is released to whom on cancellation.
A *worker* is a provider and a *client* a customer. A *job* names the work, its price in community coins and its deadline; its terms say what is released to whom on cancellation.
A person has a *location*. d > 0, an integer, and e > 0 are numbers.
A *pickup delay* is measured from the award. The *terms* of a call state a maximum pickup delay, select a bidder, set the fare and the deposit, and say how these are released.
*Second-score terms* state a maximum pickup delay T ≥ 0, a willingness to pay W(τ) = A − λτ with A, λ ≥ 0, and a deposit D ≥ 0. The award is at time t₀. A bid (p, τ) is the fare p ≥ 0 the bidder asks and the pickup delay τ ≥ 0 the bidder promises. Its *score* is W(τ) − p, and it is *admissible* iff τ ≤ T and its score is at least 0.
A *driver* is a provider and a *rider* a customer.
A *host* is a provider and a *traveller* a customer. A *listing* names a place, the nights offered and the price a night in community coins; its terms say what is released to whom on cancellation.
An *advertiser* is a member of the community who posts ads. A member's *profile* is held by the member and by no one else. An *ad* names the profile it is for, the community coins its advertiser pays for a view and for a click, the most one member may earn from it, and its *budget*, the most it pays in all.
*Posts* have a *budget*: what a post has when made, and the *cost* of a forward. Gossip has a *gossip protocol*: to which of their friends a holder may forward a post, and with what part of the rest of the budget. A person *holds* any post they made or forwarded to them.
Posts have a *test*, whether two *match*.
Bob *trusts* Wendy, a ward of Alice, when he trusts Alice. The *decision rule*, which the creator of a ward decides, says who decides for a ward and how. A ward takes an act of a party by those who decide for the ward.
A *service* is a ward operated by a machine at an address every person can reach.
An *invitation link* of Alice's is a term she signs, naming her, a rendezvous server, a serial and an expiry.
A *one-time key* is a key pair its maker uses for one meeting.
Each post carries the public key of a one-time key of its maker, and names a rendezvous server.
The budget of a post is an integer, the cost of a forward is one, and the gossip protocol is forwarding to any friend with the budget less one.
A post is a *vacancy*, stating the work and whom it seeks, or a *candidacy*, stating who its maker is and the work they seek. A vacancy and a candidacy match when each states what the other seeks.
A post is a *service*, stating work its maker does, or a *need*, stating work its maker seeks done. A service and a need match when the service is the work the need seeks.
A post is a *loan* or a *gift*, stating a thing its maker lends or gives away, or a *wish*, stating a thing its maker seeks to borrow or receive. A loan or a gift matches a wish when it is of the thing the wish seeks.
A post is a *loss*, stating a thing its maker lost, or a *find*, stating a thing its maker found. A loss and a find match when they are of the same thing.
A post is a *commute*, stating a route, its times, and whether its maker drives, rides or either. Two commutes match when their routes and times agree and one maker drives and the other rides.
A post is a *home*, stating a dwelling, when it is free, and where and when its maker seeks one. Two homes match when each is where and when the other's maker seeks.
A post is a *plan*, stating an activity, its place and its time, and whom its maker seeks for it. Two plans match when they are of the same activity, place and time and each maker is whom the other seeks.
A post is a *profile*, stating who its maker is and whom they seek. Two profiles match when each states whom the other seeks.
A *circle* is a group for the care of a person, its *patient*. A *visit* is a time at which the patient needs a person with them.
An organisation has *resources*, each with *slots*. A slot is *free* when it is not booked. A booking is *outstanding* until its slot has passed or it is cancelled. The bylaws name the *bound*, the number of outstanding bookings a participant may have.
A resource is a *room*.
A resource is the time of a *provider*, an officer of the organisation.
An organisation has *courts*, each with *slots*.
The activity is tennis, the place is a *club*, an organisation that has a fixed number of courts, and the time is a slot.
A booking is of the one who books and of a *partner*, and counts among the outstanding bookings of each.
An organisation has *rooms*, each with *slots*.
The activity is music, the place is a *studio*, an organisation that has rehearsal rooms, and the time is a slot.
A resource is a *tool*, a thing that the organisation owns and its participants use. A tool is *withdrawn* while it cannot be used.
Alice is a rider, Bob a driver, Carol a person, Dave a rendezvous server, Wendy a child, Will an organisation, Orga a community network, Issue a dispute, Ruling a ruling, Club a club. Carol and Dave are possibly one person. Bob and Carol are possibly one person. A person can be either a rider or a driver but not both.
Knowledge:1. ○ Establish: Alice may establish an identity once. Alice will make herself known by her public key, sign her acts with her private key, and be accountable for every act signed with it.
Knowledge:2. ■ Acquaint: Alice and Bob may jointly come to know each other.
Knowledge:3. ■ Introduce: Alice may introduce Carol to Bob with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other and Alice knows Carol.
Friendship:1. ○ Befriend: Alice and Bob, who trust each other and are not friends, may jointly become friends.
Friendship:2. ■ Unfriend: Alice may end her friendship with Bob.
Friendship:3. ○ Loss of Trust. Alice will end her friendship with Bob if she ceases to trust him.
Encounters:1. ■ Open place: Alice may declare the place she is in open. Close place: Alice may close it.
Encounters:2. ■ Encounter: Alice and Bob, nearby each other, who have both declared the place open, come to know each other.
Groups:1. ■ Message: Alice may send a message to her friend Bob.
Groups:2. ■ Group. Create: Alice may create a group, of which she is the leader and first member. Close: Alice may close the group by leaving it.
Groups:3. ■ Joining and Leaving. Join: Alice, the leader of a group, may add her friend Bob to it, with the consent of Bob. Remove, Leave: Either Alice or Bob may then end Bob's membership in the group, which also ends when Alice and Bob cease to be friends.
Groups:4. ■ Group messaging. Post: A member of a group may send a message to the group. Deliver: Its leader delivers it to every current member.
Overlay:1, Local Overlay:1. ■ Point friend: Alice, who does not point to her friend Bob, may point to Bob, only if either Alice points to fewer than d persons and Bob is closest to Alice among all of Alice's unpointed friends, or Bob is closer to Alice by more than e than some person pointed to by Alice.
Overlay:2, Local Overlay:2, Second-Score Auction:1. ■ Point transitive: Alice, who knows Carol and points to Bob who points to Carol, may point to Carol, only if Carol is closer to Alice by more than e than some person pointed to by Alice, and only if Carol is a driver.
Overlay:3, Local Overlay:3. ■ Unpoint: Alice, who points to Bob, may cease pointing to Bob, only if Alice points to more than d persons, with Bob furthest from Alice among them.
Labelled Overlay:1. ■ Labeled point friend: Alice, who has no Dave-pointer to her friend Bob, may add one, if Bob has a Dave-pointer.
Labelled Overlay:2, Feeds:3. ■ Labeled point transitive: Alice, who knows Carol and either has a Dave-pointer to Bob or is Bob's friend, may add a Dave-pointer to Carol, if Bob has a Dave-pointer to Carol, only if Carol knows Alice.
Labelled Overlay:3. ■ Labeled unpoint: Alice, who has a Dave-pointer to Carol, may remove it, unless Carol is Dave and her friend.
Feeds:1. ■ Post: Alice has a feed and may post to it an item, created or received.
Feeds:2. ■ Deliver: Alice, who has a Carol-pointer to Bob who knows her, receives from Bob every item of Carol's feed that Bob holds.
Guardians:1, Children:1. ◆ Enter: Alice may create a child, Wendy, and establish Wendy's identity by choosing Wendy's key pair, only if Alice is a legal parent of the minor who operates Wendy. Alice is then the creator, a parent and a friend of Wendy.
Guardians:2. ■ Parent decisions. Make parent: Those who decide for Wendy may make Bob, a friend of a parent of Wendy, a parent and a friend of Wendy, with the consent of Bob. Resign: Bob may end his guardianship of Wendy. End parent: Those who decide for Wendy, other than Bob, may end Bob's guardianship. Parent unfriend: Bob may end his friendship with Wendy, which ends his guardianship. Wendy may not end a friendship with her parent.
Guardians:3, Children:2. ■ Child and person. Child acquaint: Wendy, a child of Alice, and Bob may jointly come to know each other, only if Alice knows Bob, and with the consent of Alice. Child befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Bob with the consent of Bob and Alice, provided Wendy and Bob know each other and Alice and Bob are friends. Child end, Unfriend, Child unfriend: Wendy, Bob or Alice may end the relation of Bob and Wendy.
Guardians:4, Children:2. ■ Children. Children acquaint: Wendy, a child of Alice, and Will, a child of Bob, may jointly come to know each other, only if Alice knows Will and Bob knows Wendy, and with the consent of Alice and Bob, who know each other, Alice and Bob possibly one person. Children befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Will with the consent of Will, Alice and Bob, provided Wendy and Will know each other, Alice knows Will and is a friend of Bob, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
Guardians:5. ■ Retire: Those who decide for Wendy may retire Wendy; every guardianship and relation of Wendy then ends and Wendy can take no act.
Warded Groups:1. ■ A child's messages. Child message: Wendy may send a message to a friend (Groups:1). Child post: Wendy may send a message to a group (Groups:4).
Warded Groups:2, Children:3. ■ A child's group. Child create: Wendy may create a group (Groups:2), only with the consent of Alice, a parent of Wendy. Child close: Wendy may close it (Groups:2). Parent close: Alice, a parent of Wendy, may close it. Only a child, Will, may join the group, with the consent of Bob, a parent of Will.
Warded Groups:3. ■ Child join: Wendy may join a group (Groups:3) only with the consent of Alice, a parent of Wendy.
Children:4. ○ Of age: The creator of Wendy may declare Wendy of age, which ends every guardianship of Wendy, and Wendy is then a person. The creator will do so if the minor who operates Wendy comes of age, and not before.
Children:5. ○ A minor who is not a ward. Alice, aware that someone is a minor though not a ward, will neither befriend the minor nor let her child befriend the minor, and will report it to the minor's legal parents if she knows who they are.
Broadcast:1. ■ Forward: Alice, who holds a live broadcast, forwards it to her friend Bob, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
Broadcast:2. ■ Expire: Alice ceases to hold a broadcast that is not live.
Guardians:1. ■ Enter: Alice may create an organisation, Orga, and establish Orga's identity by choosing Orga's key pair. Alice is then the creator, an officer and a friend of Orga.
Guardians:2, Organisation:4, Backed Community Bank:1. ○ Officer decisions. Make officer: Those who decide for Orga may make Bob, a friend of an officer of Orga, an officer and a friend of Orga, with the consent of Bob, only if Bob is a participant; the decision names his role, and only if every treasurer stays backed. Resign: Bob may end his guardianship of Orga, only if every treasurer stays backed. End officer: Those who decide for Orga, other than Bob, may end Bob's guardianship, only if every treasurer stays backed. Officer unfriend: Bob may end his friendship with Orga, which ends his guardianship, only if every treasurer stays backed. Orga may not end a friendship with her officer.
Guardians:3. ■ Organisation and person. Organisation acquaint: Orga, an organisation of Alice, and Bob may jointly come to know each other. Organisation befriend: Orga may enter a relation with Bob with the consent of Bob and Alice, provided Orga and Bob know each other and Alice and Bob are friends. Organisation end, Unfriend, Organisation unfriend: Orga, Bob or Alice may end the relation of Bob and Orga.
Guardians:4. ■ Organisations. Organisations acquaint: Orga, an organisation of Alice, and Will, an organisation of Bob, may jointly come to know each other. Organisations befriend: Orga may enter a relation with Will with the consent of Will, Alice and Bob, provided Orga and Will know each other, Alice knows Will and is a friend of Bob, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
Guardians:5. ■ Retire: Those who decide for Orga may retire Orga; every guardianship and relation of Orga then ends and Orga can take no act.
Organisation:1, Community Network:3. ■ Found: Alice, or an organisation with the consent of Alice, may create Orga (Guardians:1); Alice is then its first officer, only if Alice is a member of the community.
Organisation:2. ■ Acts of the organisation. Propose: An officer, or a person the bylaws name, may propose an act of Orga. Vote: Those who decide the act may vote on it. Act: An officer the bylaws name for the act may take it for Orga after the votes decide it according to the bylaws.
Organisation:3, Constitution:1, Constitution:2, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:1, Community Network:3. ○ Participation. Join: Bob may become a participant of Orga with the consent of those who decide for Orga, only if the members decide it, and only if Bob is a member of the community. Leave, Expel: Either Bob or those who decide for Orga may end Bob's participation, and with it every role he holds, only if Bob or the members decide it, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if the Orga-coins Bob holds and the Bob-coins Orga holds have been redeemed against each other.
Organisation:5, Constitution:3. ■ Amend: Those who decide it may amend the bylaws, only if the members decide it, and the amended bylaws are egalitarian.
Organisation:6. ○ Accountability. Orga will be accountable at law for its undertakings where it is a juridical person, and every officer who decided an act of Orga will be accountable for it with Orga.
Emergencies:1. ■ Personal emergency: Alice may broadcast a personal emergency, provided she has no live personal emergency of her own.
Emergencies:2. ■ Village emergency: Alice, an officer of Orga, may broadcast a village emergency.
Emergencies:3. ■ Emergency forward: Alice, a participant of Orga, may forward a live village emergency of Orga that she holds to Bob, a participant of Orga, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
Emergencies:4. ■ Resolve: Alice may broadcast the resolution of her personal emergency.
Emergencies:5. ■ Answer: Bob, who holds a live personal emergency, may broadcast an answer to it that says the help he will give.
Emergencies:6. ○ Help. Bob will give the help he answered.
Notices:1. ■ Notice: Alice, an officer of Orga, may broadcast a notice.
Notices:2. ■ Notice forward: Alice, a participant of Orga, may forward a live notice of Orga that she holds to Bob, a participant of Orga, who does not hold it; Bob then holds it.
Notes:1. ■ Issue: Alice may issue Alice-notes.
Notes:2, Denominated Currencies:2, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Swap: Alice and Bob, who know each other, may jointly swap notes they hold, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Notes:3, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Pay: Alice may pay notes she holds to Bob, whom she knows, with his consent, only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Notes:4, Denominated Currencies:2, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Escrow. Deposit: Alice may deposit notes with Carol for Bob, on a condition the three agree, with the consent of Carol, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins. Release: Carol and Bob may jointly release them to Bob, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins. Return: Carol and Alice may jointly return them to Alice, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins. Carol will release them only if the condition is met, and return them only if it fails. Each act is between two parties who know each other.
Coins:1, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Pay issuer: Notes:3, without the consent of Bob, if the coins are Bob-coins, only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Coins:2, Denominated Currencies:2, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Redeem: Alice may redeem a Bob-coin she holds against any coin held by Bob, whom she knows, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Coins:3. ○ Pricing. Alice will price her offerings in Alice-coins and accept them in payment at those prices.
Bonds:1, Denominated Currencies:2, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Redeem: Alice may redeem a Bob-coin, or a mature Bob-bond, she holds against any coin or bond held by Bob, whom she knows, only if the coins and bonds are of one denomination, and only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Denominated Coins:1. ■ Issue: Alice may issue Alice-coins denominated by a fiat currency.
Denominated Coins:2. ○ Denomination. A Dollar-denominated Alice-coin is due now; Alice will redeem it on presentation, by a Dollar-denominated coin the bearer accepts or by one Dollar.
Denominated Coins:3. ○ Pricing. Alice will accept Dollar-denominated Alice-coins in payment for her offerings at one Dollar each.
Denominated Currencies:1. ■ Issue denominated bond: Alice may issue Alice-bonds denominated by a fiat currency, of a maturity later than the current date.
Denominated Currencies:3. ■ Accept: Alice may accept Dollar-denominated Carol-coins in payment up to a limit of her choosing, if she holds a Dollar-denominated Carol-coin or Carol-bond; each such coin paid to Alice counts against the limit, and Alice may accept again.
Denominated Currencies:4, Backed Community Bank:1, Mutual Credit:3. ○ Pay accepted coins: Alice may pay Bob, whom she knows, coins she holds that Bob accepts, only if every treasurer stays backed, and only if every member is then in the red by at most 1000 coins.
Community Bank:1, Backed Community Bank:2. ■ Draw: Alice, a treasurer, may swap Alice-coins for Orga-coins, only if Alice stays backed.
Community Bank:2, Backed Community Bank:4. ○ Fiat redemption. Any treasurer will redeem an Orga-coin Bob holds against one Dollar, from the account while it holds Dollars, and from a treasurer if it holds none.
Backed Community Bank:3. ◆ Record: Alice, a treasurer, may pay Dollars into the account, and the treasurers may then jointly record them as paid in by Alice.
Disputes:1. ■ Raise: Alice may raise Issue with Bob in Orga to Carol, provided Orga has Alice as a participant, Orga has Bob as a participant and Orga has Carol in the role Arbiter.
Disputes:2. ■ Decide: Carol may decide Issue between Alice and Bob in Orga with the ruling Ruling.
Disputes:3. ○ Abide. Alice and Bob will abide by the decision of Carol.
Warnings:1. ■ Warn: Alice may warn Bob in Orga of an incident, provided Alice is an officer of Orga and Orga has Bob as a participant.
Warnings:2. ■ Answer: Bob may answer a warning to him.
Warnings:3. ■ Withdrawal. Withdraw: Alice may withdraw her warning. Annul: Those who decide for Orga may annul a warning.
Warnings:4. ■ Expel: Organisation:3 Expel, only if Orga holds warnings to Bob of two persons, each given more than seven days before. Officer expel: Organisation:3 Officer expel, only if Orga holds warnings to Bob of two persons, each given more than seven days before.
Works:1. ■ Approve: Those who decide for Orga may approve a work, with the consent of Bob, its contractor; its price is then locked.
Works:2. ◆ Complete: Bob may attest that he completed an approved work.
Works:3. ◆ Accept: Carol, the supervisor of an approved work, may attest that Bob, its contractor, completed it; its price is then released to Bob.
Works:4. ■ Reject: Carol may reject a work that Bob attested he completed, giving her reason.
Works:5. ■ Cancel: Those who decide for Orga may cancel an approved work, with the consent of Bob; its price is then released to Bob and to Orga as agreed.
Works:6. ■ Supervise: Those who decide for Orga may make Carol, an officer of Orga, the supervisor of an approved work.
Works:7. ■ Arbitration. Raise: Either Bob or those who decide for Orga may raise an approved work, not yet raised, to an arbiter, Dave. Arbitrate: Dave may then decide the release of its price to Bob and to Orga.
Mutual Credit:2. ■ Redeem member's coin: Bob, a member, may redeem an Alice-coin he holds against an Orga-coin, provided Alice is a member.
Joint Accounts:1. ■ Open account: Alice and Bob, who know each other, may jointly open a joint account, under a new name of Alice's.
Joint Accounts:2. ■ Account deposit: Either of them may move coins they hold into their joint account.
Joint Accounts:3. ■ Withdraw: Alice and Bob may jointly move coins from their joint account to either of them.
Community Network:1. ■ Set stake: Those who decide for Orga may set S.
Community Network:2, Lodging:5. ■ Arbitration. Raise: Either Alice or Bob, the parties to a dispute, may raise it to an arbiter, Carol, only before checkout, and by Alice only if she is checked in. Arbitrate: Carol may then decide the release of the locked coins to Alice and to Bob, less the fee the terms set, which is released to her.
Community Network:4. ○ Loss of membership. Those who decide for Orga will end Bob's participation in Orga if he ceases to be a member of the community.
Recommendations:1, Community Market:5, Gigs:6, Lodging:6. ◆ Recommend: Alice may recommend Bob, whom she knows, for something, a skill or a service, once for each thing; Bob keeps the recommendation, where Alice recommends Bob for the good after delivery, and where Alice recommends Bob for the work after acceptance, and where Alice recommends Bob for the stay after checkout.
Recommendations:2. ■ Show: Bob may show a recommendation he holds to Carol, whom he knows, once; Carol then sees who recommended Bob and for what.
Recommendations:3. ■ Withdraw: Alice may withdraw a recommendation; it is then gone from Bob and from everyone Bob showed it to, and Alice may not make it again.
Community Market:1. ■ Listing. Post: Bob, a seller, may post a listing to the buyers he points to. Pass: A buyer may pass it to the buyers they point to. Withdraw listing: Bob may withdraw it.
Community Market:2. ■ Order: Alice, a buyer, may order the good from Bob with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other; Alice's payment and the deposit the terms set for Bob, on top of his stake, are then locked.
Community Market:3. ◆ Deliver: Alice may attest that the good was delivered to her, and the payment and the deposit are then released to Bob.
Community Market:4. ■ Cancel: Alice or Bob may cancel the order before delivery, and the payment and the deposit are then released to Alice and to Bob as the terms say.
Gigs:1. ■ Job. Post: Alice, a client, may post a job to the workers she points to. Pass: A worker may pass it to the workers they point to. Withdraw job: Alice may withdraw it.
Gigs:2. ■ Engage: Alice may engage Bob, a worker, for the job with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other; Alice's payment and the deposit the terms set for Bob, on top of his stake, are then locked.
Gigs:3. ◆ Deliver: Bob may attest that he delivered the work to Alice.
Gigs:4. ■ Acceptance. Accept work: Alice may accept delivered work, and the payment and the deposit are then released to Bob. Reject: Alice may reject it, raising a dispute (Community Network:2).
Gigs:5. ■ Cancelling. Cancel: Alice or Bob may cancel the engagement before delivery, and the payment and the deposit are then released to Alice and to Bob as the terms say. Lapse: If no delivery is attested by the deadline, Alice may cancel and both are then released to her.
Auction:1. ■ Call. Call: Alice, who has no open call and no ride, may call for bids on a ride from the persons Alice points to, stating the pickup point, the destination, the bidding period and the terms. Forward call: Each of them forwards the call to the persons they point to.
Auction:2. ■ Bid: Bob, who received the call, may bid a fare and a pickup delay before the bidding period ends; Alice may not open a bid before then.
Auction:3, Second-Score Auction:2, Rides:1. ■ Award. Award: After the bidding period ends, Alice may award the ride to the bidder the terms select among the bidders who have no ride, at the fare the terms set; Alice's fare and the deposit the terms set for Bob are then locked, where the terms select the bidder whose admissible bid has the highest score, ties broken as the terms say, or no bidder if no bid is admissible, and only if the fare and the deposit are in community coins, Alice holds the fare, and Bob holds the deposit on top of his stake, and the fare and the deposit are then locked between the provider Bob and the customer Alice (Community Network:2). Close: If the terms select no bidder, Alice may close the call, where the terms select the bidder whose admissible bid has the highest score, ties broken as the terms say, or no bidder if no bid is admissible. They set the fare P = W(τ) − s₂, where τ is that bid's pickup delay and s₂ is the highest score among the other admissible bids, or 0 if there is none, and they set the deposit D.
Auction:4. ■ Pickup: The pickup is recorded when Alice and Bob are both at the pickup point.
Auction:5, Second-Score Auction:3. ■ Arrive: When Alice and Bob are both at the destination, either of them may claim the release of the fare and the deposit, which are then released to Alice and to Bob as the terms say, where the refund min{P, λδ} is released to Alice, and the rest of the fare and the deposit to Bob, with δ = max{0, t_pickup − t₀ − τ}.
Auction:6, Second-Score Auction:4. ■ Cancel: If no pickup is recorded within the maximum pickup delay, Alice may cancel; the fare and the deposit are then released to Alice and to Bob as the terms say, where the fare and the deposit are released to Alice if Alice was at the pickup point from t₀ to t₀ + T, and otherwise the fare to Alice and the deposit to Bob.
Auction:7. ■ Withdraw: Alice may withdraw her open call before the bidding period ends.
Lodging:1. ■ Listing. Post: Bob, a host, may post a listing to the travellers he points to. Pass: A traveller may pass it to the travellers they point to. Withdraw listing: Bob may withdraw it.
Lodging:2. ■ Book: Alice, a traveller, may book nights of Bob's listing with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other; Alice's payment for them and the deposit the terms set for Bob, on top of his stake, are then locked.
Lodging:3. ■ Check-in and checkout. Check in: Alice may record her check-in when she is at the place on the first night. Check out: Alice may record her checkout when she leaves it after the last night; the payment and the deposit are then released to Bob.
Lodging:4. ■ Cancelling. Cancel: Alice or Bob may cancel a booking before the first night, and the payment and the deposit are then released to Alice and to Bob as the terms say. No-show: If no check-in is recorded on the first night while Alice is at the place, she may cancel and both are then released to her.
Ads:1. ■ Posting. Post: Bob, an advertiser, may post an ad to the members he points to; its budget, which he holds, is then locked. Pass: A member may pass it to the members they point to.
Ads:2. ■ Show: Alice, a member, is shown an ad she received if it is for her profile.
Ads:3. ◆ Viewing and clicking. View, Click: Alice may attest that she viewed, or clicked, an ad shown to her, and the ad's budget then pays her its coins for the view or the click, up to the most one member may earn from it.
Gossip:1. ■ Post: Alice may make a post.
Gossip:2. ■ Tell: Alice who holds a post, the budget of which covers the cost, may forward it to her friend Bob with a part of the rest of the budget, both according to the gossip protocol.
Matching:1. ■ Return: Bob, who holds two matching posts, one from Alice, forwards to Alice the second post.
Matching:2, Anonymous Matching:1. ■ Meet: Alice and Carol, both holding matching posts one made by Alice and one made by Carol, may jointly come to know each other, only by Anonymous Rendezvous:1 with the one-time keys of the two posts, at the rendezvous server named by the post whose public key has the smaller hash.
Guardians:1. ■ Enter: Alice may create a ward, Wendy, and establish Wendy's identity by choosing Wendy's key pair. Alice is then the creator, a guardian and a friend of Wendy.
Guardians:2. ■ Guardian decisions. Make guardian: Those who decide for Wendy may make Bob, a friend of a guardian of Wendy, a guardian and a friend of Wendy, with the consent of Bob. Resign: Bob may end his guardianship of Wendy. End guardian: Those who decide for Wendy, other than Bob, may end Bob's guardianship. Guardian unfriend: Bob may end his friendship with Wendy, which ends his guardianship. Wendy may not end a friendship with her guardian.
Guardians:3. ■ Ward and person. Ward acquaint: Wendy, a ward of Alice, and Bob may jointly come to know each other. Ward befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Bob with the consent of Bob and Alice, provided Wendy and Bob know each other and Alice and Bob are friends. Ward end, Unfriend, Ward unfriend: Wendy, Bob or Alice may end the relation of Bob and Wendy.
Guardians:4. ■ Wards. Wards acquaint: Wendy, a ward of Alice, and Will, a ward of Bob, may jointly come to know each other. Wards befriend: Wendy may enter a relation with Will with the consent of Will, Alice and Bob, provided Wendy and Will know each other, Alice knows Will and is a friend of Bob, Alice and Bob possibly one person.
Rendezvous:1. ■ Open server: Carol may make her service Dave a rendezvous server.
Rendezvous:2. ■ Invite by link: Alice may register with Dave an invitation link of hers that names Dave, with a new serial.
Rendezvous:3. ■ Use link: Bob may present to Dave an invitation link of Alice's registered with Dave that has not expired; Dave then gives Alice Bob's address and Bob Alice's, and the link is spent.
Rendezvous:4. ■ Reconnection. Present: Alice and Bob, who are friends, may each present to Dave the other's signature over their friendship. Match: Dave then gives each the address of the other.
Anonymous Rendezvous:1. ■ Meet. Present: Alice and Bob, each holding a one-time key and knowing the public key of the other's, may each present to Dave the two public keys, signed with their own. Match: Dave then gives each the address of the other.
Library:1. ◆ Shelve: Alice may put a thing of her own on her shelf, under a new name of hers.
Library:2. ■ Lend: Alice may lend Bob a thing from her shelf until a day later than the current date, with the consent of Bob, provided Alice and Bob know each other; it then leaves the shelf, and Bob holds it.
Library:3. ■ Return: Bob may return a borrowed thing; it then goes back on Alice's shelf.
Library:4. ○ On time. Bob will return a borrowed thing by the agreed day.
Care:1. ◆ Open: Alice may create a circle (Groups:2) for her own care, or for the care of Carol, attesting that Carol asked her to.
Care:2. ■ Ask: A member of a circle may post a visit to it.
Care:3. ○ Take: Bob, a member of the circle, may take a posted visit. Bob will make the visit, or release it in time for another member to take it.
Care:4. ■ Release: Bob, the leader or the patient may release a visit Bob took; it is then posted again.
Care:5. ◆ Report. Made: Bob may attest to the circle that he made a visit he took. Missed: The leader or the patient may attest to the circle that a visit taken was missed.
Care:6. ■ End: The patient may close a circle for their care.
Booking:1, Tools:5. ■ Book: Alice, a participant of Orga with fewer outstanding bookings than the bound, may book any free slot of a resource of Orga, only if the tool is not withdrawn.
Booking:2. ■ Cancel: Alice may cancel her booking.
Booking:1, Tennis Courts:1. ■ Book: Alice, a participant of Orga with fewer outstanding bookings than the bound, may book any free slot of a court of Orga, by Alice and Carol jointly, each a participant of the Club with fewer outstanding bookings than the bound; Carol is the partner of the booking.
Tennis Courts:2. ■ Organisation and ward. Organisation ward acquaint: Club, an organisation, and Wendy, a ward, may jointly come to know each other.
Tennis Courts:3. ■ Cancel: Booking:2; the cancel frees the slot and ends the partner's part in the booking.
Tennis Courts:4. ■ Withdraw: Carol may withdraw as the partner of a booking, which stays the booking of the one who booked.
Tennis Courts:5. ■ Partner: Alice and Carol may jointly make Carol the partner of a booking of Alice that has no partner, Carol a participant of the Club with fewer outstanding bookings than the bound; so a partner is replaced, the old one withdrawing, while the slot stays booked.
Booking:1. ■ Book: Alice, a participant of Orga with fewer outstanding bookings than the bound, may book any free slot of a room of Orga.
Rehearsal Rooms:1. ■ Organisation and ward. Organisation ward acquaint: Orga, an organisation, and Wendy, a ward, may jointly come to know each other.
Tools:1. ◆ Hand over: Carol, an officer of Orga, and Alice, who booked a tool, may jointly attest that Alice took it for her slot, provided no one holds the tool and it is not withdrawn. Alice then holds it.
Tools:2. ○ Return. Alice will return the tool to an officer of Orga by the end of her slot, as she took it.
Tools:3. ◆ Take back: Carol, an officer of Orga, may attest that Alice returned the tool she holds.
Tools:4. ■ Withdraw: Carol, an officer of Orga, may withdraw a tool. Restore: Carol may restore a withdrawn tool.
